posts.title: Patch notes: Alpha 0.3.7
posts.excerpt: Four missile types with new launchers, three thruster types, weapon platforms that fight, smarter NPC wings, a new-look Sigma-17, and new rocks, props and buoys everywhere.
posts.body:
**New in the game**

*Ships and guns*

- New thruster types in Mk I–V: Burst (Kestrel) is strong but thirsty, Marathon (Albatross) lasts longest, Vector (Dragonfly) strafes and turns better.
- Thruster dealers sell all three types; early-access dealers carry Mk I–III by standing, and no dealer sells Mk V.
- Missiles come in four types: homing Stalker, straight-flying Organ, the new six-rocket Circus swarm, and Static EMP.
- Organ launchers hold 150 missiles at a third of the old price.
- Launchers fit gun mounts by mark: Mk I–II small, Mk III–IV medium, Mk V large for heavy fighters.
- Launchers have their own models that aim like turrets: Talon (homing), Carillon (ballistic), Hanabi (swarm) and Donner (EMP).
- Each missile type has its own model, drive glow and trail.
- The Defender now flies as the Liberty Navy's, with Navy lettering and Liberty's crest on its wings and nose.
- Ship editor: place up to 8 faction crests anywhere on your hull, then size, turn or remove them.

*Combat*

- No more lock-on: R fires every missile launcher at once.
- Homing missiles fly straight briefly after launch, then seek with a wider cone and more speed.
- Your homing missiles do 2.5x NPC damage, ballistic and swarm 1.5x; two EMP hits strip a same-mark light fighter's shield.
- Circus rockets burst near foes and spare your allies; swarm rounds fire every 2.5 seconds.
- NPCs now use afterburners, with a thrust store like yours, and lead their straight missiles like gun shots.
- NPC fighters bank into hard turns and fly level otherwise, instead of fighting on their side.
- NPC wings focus the most hurt enemy, flank their target, and pull damaged ships back under cover.
- Open-world wings may flee after losing their leader or half their ships; Police and Navy wings call for help.
- Weapon platforms fight with buyable weapons against hostiles and anyone who shoots them, and return 30 minutes after being destroyed.
- Destroyed weapon platforms break apart in a big blast, leaving burning wreck pieces behind.
- The small weapon platform carries 8 turrets; Liberty's big platform gains 4 gun turrets and twice the hit points.
- Turrets on platforms and NPC ships fire only where their barrels can point, not through their own hulls.
- West Point fires back with turrets and missiles; stations take hits but can't be destroyed.
- NPC guns now recoil, and NPC two-part turrets pitch their barrels.
- Every 10% of hull lost wears 5 condition points off a random mounted item.

*Jobs and missions*

- Each character now has its own job board, and taking a job rolls a new board.
- Defend jobs show a new Hold the line crest.

*Trading and loot*

- The nav map's base cards have a MARKET tab with known buy and sell prices; the system card shows the best ones.
- With Market Contacts, the map's market prices show as LIVE and refresh while the map is open.
- Outfitters offer REPAIR HULL for a damaged ship; Thrifty Repairs applies.

*World*

- Floating props are rebuilt at three times the size: tank rows and crosses, Detroit's Communications Satellite, wrecks and storage depots.
- Storage depots have open cargo bays stacked with containers, with rims in the cargo pod colour code.
- California has 1.7 km ice crystal spires, and Tahoe has ice crystals up to 300 m.
- The Badlands are a forest of dark rock shards up to 700 m tall.
- Asteroid fields use new, lighter grey rocks, each a little lighter or darker than the next.
- A 1 km rock spire rises between Pittsburgh and Maine, and four ice rocks surround Willard Research Station.
- Sigma-17 has a new look: green and blue suns, the Kunashir and Nemuro nebulae, and Kurile as an island ocean world.
- New designs for Liberty's big weapon platform, the pirates' asteroid platforms and the small weapon platform.
- New nav, hazard and race buoys with blinking lamps; gravity buoys are gone.
- Liberty's livery is now a warm off-white with navy and gunmetal and no gold; Trenton takes West Point's look.
- Liberty's jump gate has a new surface with plating and grime.
- Manhattan shows the LSF crest beside the pad, and Liberty's crest replaces the gold star in the lounge, bar, reception and ready room.
- Six new guests sit in the Liberty stations' bar, and the bartender wears a waistcoat suit.
- People in base rooms move naturally, look at whoever they talk to, blink, and talk with moving faces.
- The flight instructor now stands like a Navy officer, and Manhattan's officers wear uniforms.

*Interface*

- Pictures on item tiles for droppers, flares, nanobots, shield batteries, thrusters, mines and missiles; empty slots show a dimmed picture.
- Base screen, flight menu, outfitter and start menu buttons show pictures instead of line icons.
- Click a waypoint marker to target it, then fly there with Go To.
- The outfitter shows stats by item kind, compares only like items, adds infocards and scrolls.
- Launchers and missiles show their type in colour: homing blue, ballistic orange, swarm white, EMP red; cruise disruptors purple.
- Launchers carry line names such as Talon Mk III "Moonstalker"; storage lists ammo for your ship first.
- After selling from the outfitter's cargo bay, the next row is selected so you can keep clicking SELL.
- The missile lock marker is gone; your selected target is the lock.
- New report form in the Flight Menu for bugs, feedback and reporting players, with a screenshot attached.
- The start menu overlooks Trenton Outpost, Manhattan and the ice ring star, with ships flying past.
- The loading screen stays up until the system is ready, shows the title card and has new pictures.

*Graphics and performance*

- New Options > Graphics > All stars switch: show every star or only those visible to the naked eye.
- Sharper sun shadows at Medium and High quality.
- Rocks stay sharp at any size and distance.
- Lights on stations, platforms, buoys and ships glow from afar.
- Missile blasts are lighter, and a swarm round shows two blasts instead of six.
- EMP-jammed hulls crackle with red lightning, and the Donner bursts in a red EMP pulse.
- The character screen and the docking bay with bar guests run faster.

*Sound*

- The Hanabi launcher fires with a cannon shot and its rockets whoosh away.
- The Donner's EMP pulse goes off with a thunder crack.

*Multiplayer*

- Weapon platforms fight in multiplayer too.
- Other players see the crests you place on your hull.

**New and changed in the [wiki](#/wiki)**

- New ship **[Piranha](#/wiki/ships/piranha)**: Now in the wiki.
- New ship **[Transport](#/wiki/ships/transport)**: Now in the wiki.
- New ship **[Large Transport](#/wiki/ships/large-transport)**: Now in the wiki.

- New ship **[Barracuda](#/wiki/ships/barracuda)**: Now in the wiki.
- New system **[Sigma-17](#/wiki/systems/sigma-17)**: Its own look, and several suns per system.
- New weapon **[Barrager](#/wiki/weapons/barrager)**: Now in the wiki.
- New weapon **[Scrapstorm](#/wiki/weapons/scrapstorm)**: Now in the wiki.

- New station **[Communications Satellite](#/wiki/stations/communications-satellite)**: Now in the wiki.
- New station **[](#/wiki/stations/)**: Space props 3x FL's size from the station pack.
- New station **[Weapons Platform](#/wiki/stations/weapons-platform)**: Now in the wiki.
- New station **[Navigation Buoy](#/wiki/stations/navigation-buoy)**: Now in the wiki.
- New station **[Hazard Buoy](#/wiki/stations/hazard-buoy)**: Now in the wiki.
- New station **[Sigma-17 –> Sigma-19](#/wiki/stations/sigma-17-sigma-19)**: Now in the wiki.
- New station **[Weapon Platform](#/wiki/stations/weapon-platform)**: Alex's design for Liberty's big platform.
- **[Defender](#/wiki/ships/defender)**: Defender as the Liberty Navy's, Liberty's national crest on its wings and nose.
- **[California](#/wiki/systems/california)**: California's layout map.
- **[Orbital Station](#/wiki/stations/orbital-station)**: Rebuilt Trenton, the orbital station, Liberty's trade lane ring, the berth doors and Willard without gold.
- No longer in the wiki (stations): New York –> California.

posts.title: How I make a new Ship in 2 hours using AI
posts.excerpt: With proper systems you can get new ships into your game in hours!
posts.body:
I've recently been asked what my workflow for adding new ships is.

I have been a dev in my day job for 20 years, so EVERYTHING is systems based. Especially with AI this is ABSOLUTELY necessary :)

This is taken straight from Discord.

# The Workflow
Say the Drone Freighter for Kusari (which isnt in yet).

This was the prompt in Tripo AI (which used chatGPT image generation):
"Create a cool japanese style freighter space ship. Not a huge hauler. Medium sized. Visible cargo. Make the wings look like dragon wings or something"

Then I had it created like 8-16 different images. Lots of them are ass, so you gotta go with numbers.

![](images/uploads/2026-11-08-image-mw7n7ucb.jpg)

Then I pick one and tell Tripo to render it as a 3D model.

Now this is a shitshow because its guessing a lot from the image. You can add different angles, so sometimes I ask grok to give me different angles of the reference ship. Sometimes it works right away
I chose this:

![](images/uploads/2026-11-08-image-2-mw7n8c33.jpg)

It then creates multiple versions of this in wireframe 3D. Many of them suck or have tons of holes. So its a numbers game again until you find a good one

![](images/uploads/2026-11-08-image-mw7n8snz.jpg)

This is the result.
Now this has still a tons of bugs at this point. And this is where I have created by trial and error, a 9 step part for Claude.AI to go over the model, look for holes with a magenta background. Mirror starboard to portside or vice versa if its asymmetrical. Remove unnecessary stuff and place guns yourself.

Then it goes for the textures, removing AI scriblles, fixing issues, and building multiple layers for liveries and decals as well as the frost in ice clouds 
Sometimes these are wrong, so I need to place them myself, or tell the AI where to do it
So through try and error, eventually you get to a ship that looks good. I check it then ingame. Tell the AI to fix things, etc

# SYSTEMS, EVERYWHERE

You see, ive been a dev for 20 years, so EVERYTHING is systems based.

I have developed systems for the ships, the systems, the guns, the suns, the planets. All of it follows an outlined system the AI just works with

Which is again, where I say, AI doesnt solve your issues, it just makes your work a lot faster
But with this I can basically get a ship into the game within roughly 3-4 hours fully playable
which is still insane

I did the same for weapon platforms or even big planetsized rocks which I recently added. Although for those we use texture tiling, because the tripo 4k texture gets stretched a lot otherwise

Now for capital ships, its a whole nother work. You will have to split it up into multiple parts. THats how I made the NPC Transport ship which is massive. Front, center, and back, each done differently in Tripo, otherwise the textures get blurry af.

Then stitched together.

Took me a whole day for this one, but wurth it

![](images/uploads/2026-11-08-screenshot-20261108-105002-mw7niuuv.jpg)

posts.title: Patch notes: Alpha 0.3.6
posts.excerpt: Pirate start: begin unlawful at Buffalo Base. Redesigned Mule, Bloodhound, Dromedary, Valkyrie and Barracuda, custom engine colours, patrol scans of pirates, and multiplayer leaderboards.
posts.body:
**New in the game**

*Ships and guns*

- Mule redesigned: new hull, glass canopy, four exhausts that fill their openings, MULE and crest on the nose.
- Mule now has 3750 hull, 150 cargo hold, 20 bots and batteries, and Rochester sells it too.
- Bloodhound redesigned, with FACTORY pirate paint or plain gunmetal UNFLAGGED livery and glowing red lamps.
- Dromedary redesigned as the Zoners' civilian freighter, with cargo stacked in side bays.
- Valkyrie redesigned as a 25 m Rheinland heavy fighter, with recessed exhausts and louvred intake vents.
- Rheinland ships get long deep-red engine flames with lightning crackling round them.
- Barracuda redesigned at its original 18 m length, with wingtip lights and BARRACUDA on the prongs.
- Wolfhound gets new intake fans and a ring of amber lamps in each duct that brighten with throttle.
- Pick each ship's engine design and its colours in flight and cruise in the hangar's Ship Editor.
- Cargo carried on the hull fills its bays far better, so a full hold shows many more crates.
- Countermeasure droppers are now Mirage Mk I, II and III, firing Mirage Flare Mk I, II and III.

*Combat*

- Flares now divert cruise disruptors as well as missiles. Torpedoes ignore flares.
- An incoming cruise disruptor gets its own teal warning showing its distance.
- Lawful patrols hostile to you scan your hold before firing and order it dropped. Refusing or fleeing means a fight.
- If you drop your cargo they spare you for two minutes, but now and then they attack anyway.
- Bounty hunters always attack on sight. Patrols attack ships with empty holds without scanning.

*Characters and progression*

- Choose a lawful or unlawful start when creating a character. The story is played as lawful.
- Unlawful start: docked at Buffalo Base in a Starflier, friendly with Rogues and Lane Hackers, wanted by the navies.

*Interface*

- The Trader shows the selected good's picture on its card.
- Hangar: switch the ship view to a selected weapon, shown live and turnable.
- The ship dealer's stats bars now compare against the best buyable ship of every class.
- Shields show a picture of their type: a dome for Bulwark, a hex plate for Flux, a shell for Deflector.
- Jump drives show their own picture on item tiles.

*Sound*

- The Neural Net now announces when your cruise is disrupted.

*Multiplayer*

- Leaderboards for kills, bounties, biggest haul, trade profit and systems charted, weekly or all time.
- Sydney at a Liberty station's reception opens the leaderboards. The nav map has a filter for her stations.
- The system map shows who first found a jump hole or loot wreck, and when.

**New and changed in the [wiki](#/wiki)**

- New ship **[Piranha](#/wiki/ships/piranha)**: Now in the wiki.
- New ship **[Transport](#/wiki/ships/transport)**: Now in the wiki.
- New ship **[Large Transport](#/wiki/ships/large-transport)**: Now in the wiki.
- New ship **[Dagger](#/wiki/ships/dagger)**: Now in the wiki.
- New ship **[Wolfhound](#/wiki/ships/wolfhound)**: Wolfhound intakes after Alex's look.
- New ship **[Mule](#/wiki/ships/mule)**: Mule redesign.
- New ship **[Bloodhound](#/wiki/ships/bloodhound)**: Bloodhound redesign.
- New ship **[Dromedary](#/wiki/ships/dromedary)**: Dromedary redesign.
- New ship **[Valkyrie](#/wiki/ships/valkyrie)**: The port wing mirrored over the starboard one, 25 m across, the stern's flat plates recessed into exhausts, the pods' sloped exhaust floors squared to the thrust, the four intakes recessed and louvred.
- New ship **[Barracuda](#/wiki/ships/barracuda)**: A bigger Piranha at the original's 18.1 m.
- New weapon **[Barrager](#/wiki/weapons/barrager)**: Now in the wiki.
- New weapon **[Scrapstorm](#/wiki/weapons/scrapstorm)**: Now in the wiki.
- New weapon **[Azrael](#/wiki/weapons/azrael)**: Now in the wiki.

posts.title: Patch notes: Alpha 0.3.5
posts.excerpt: Escort and hold-the-line jobs, a level earned by flying with perks, a full loot overhaul, Manhattan's city surface, and new ship and gun models.
posts.body:
**New in the game**

*Ships and guns*

- The Patriot has a new police model with a police light bar, strobes and glass canopy.
- The Defender is now 22 m long, with a navy-and-gold LSF livery, cleaner nose line and crest.
- The Startracker's boom strips glow cleanly, and it has one rectangular afterburner nozzle with a matching flame.
- The Piranha is redesigned, with glass side windows, PIRANHA markings and teal engines.
- The Dagger is redesigned, with a pirate factory livery, a plain gunmetal look and dark orange Ember engines.
- The Wolfhound is redesigned, with turning intake fans and Ember engines.
- Transports are redesigned in small and large versions, with honeycomb intakes and ten teal ring engines.
- Freighters and Transports now show their cargo in their bays: containers, crates, tanks or gas.
- New models for the Justice, Starbeam, Lavablade, Stunpulse, Azrael, Barrager, Death's Hand, Reaper and Scorpion.
- Guns carry a glowing level light: blue for low marks, amber for higher marks, red for signature Epics.
- The Starbeam, Lavablade, Azrael, Death's Hand, Reaper and Scorpion fire bolts of their own; the Barrager fires the Starbeam's.
- The Stunpulse crackles with constant lightning between its claws.
- Each gun line has one name with marks counted straight through, such as Justice Mk I to V.
- Each faction's signature Epic is its line's top mark with its own name, such as Vengeance.
- Mark pips show a gun's mark in the outfitter and inventory.
- Turrets carry their line's gun on a base in that gun's colour.
- Player guns and turrets have new infocards describing their family, turret role and signature drops.
- The 15 Legendary story guns each have their own trait, from Chain lightning and Spreading fire to Judgement.
- The hangar's new SHIP EDITOR combines livery, paint and a worn or clean finish, with a live preview.
- Name your ship in the SHIP EDITOR; the name shows in the hangar, dealers, inventory and to other players.
- NPC ships now show their hull lettering and the crest of the faction flying them.
- Ship class badges have new crest artwork.

*Combat*

- Shooting a friendly ship builds its anger: past a warning, its whole group turns on you.
- Groups that like you, and also like a ship you fight, now take a side, with radio calls.
- NPC fighters choose maneuvers from their ship's own tactics: buzzing, trailing, strafing, evading and engine kills.
- NPC aim follows a new accuracy cone, with no aim error against a nearly still ship.
- Mines reworked: they arm in half a second, last 4 minutes, drift toward enemies and survive stray bolts.
- New mine types: EMP mines jam and stop cruise, Singularity mines pull ships into a black hole.
- Mines have a new spiked model with lights that glow by mine type.
- Freighters carry twice as many mines.
- Ship explosions now match the size of the ship.
- Dying wears every item mounted on your ship by 20 condition points.

*Jobs and missions*

- New job: Escort a convoy to another base, even through gates to California; raids come along the way.
- New job: Hold the line, defending a stranded convoy against waves of raiders.
- Escorts and held lines pay by the share of the convoy that survives.
- Mission commander, convoy captain and raid leader speak voiced lines in the comm window.
- Jobs now come in 2-3 waves; the next wave arrives when the last is nearly down.
- In assassination jobs, the target leads the last wave.
- Jobs farther from the base pay up to double.
- Pay now rises properly with a job's danger.
- Leave a battle by over 15 km and a 20-second countdown starts before the job fails.
- The mission commander gives objectives and battle calls, and announces each job's result.
- A completed job shows a VICTORY screen with the paying faction's crest, pay and giver.
- Map job bar: SET COURSE, ABORT MISSION, and LAUNCH NOW when docked; the job waypoint stays marked.
- Routes re-plan from where your ship is, always marking the next lane ring, gate or goal.
- Jobs above your level drop more and better loot, shown as OUTRANKED on the board.
- Job board cards are larger, with the giver's crest and the job kind's crest.
- The job board shows each job's waves, level range and distance.
- Job dealers show a briefcase icon instead of a gun.

*Trading and loot*

- Loot crates look their rarity, from cargo boxes to glowing capsules; Epic drops nearby get a banner.
- Epic and Legendary crates are sealed: get within 500 m and hold the beam 3 seconds.
- Tap B for a loot overlay listing crates by rarity and value, with tractor, scrap and never-take options.
- Hold B to take the best loot in range until the hold is full.
- Set which rarities to collect automatically, and items to never take, in Options or the loot overlay.
- Equipment and ammo now take hold space.
- Scrap equipment and ammo into scrap metal, from your hold or a crate in range.
- Looted equipment comes damaged and works worse until repaired; dealers pay less for it.
- New REPAIR button at dealers restores items to full condition.
- Legendaries drop only rarely from kills; your chance grows with each kill since the last one.
- Every drop is rarer the higher its rarity.
- Loot from kills is personal: each player who helped gets their own crates.
- 41 new smuggled trade goods, mostly sold and bought at pirate bases and Freeports.
- Six new Epic contraband goods come only as loot from pirates, Zoners and loot wrecks.
- Traffic freighters carry goods their routes trade, and drop them when destroyed.
- Every commodity now has its own picture, and gun tiles show the gun's picture.
- Item tiles are tinted by rarity.
- The outfitter's BUY puts gear into the cargo bay when no slot is free.

*Characters and progression*

- Your level is now earned by flying: kills, jobs, trade profit and discoveries, worth more in dangerous places.
- At levels 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25, pick one of three utility perks in Player Status.
- Perks include Long Tractor, Thrifty Repairs, Insured Hold, Salvager, Diplomat, Well Connected and more.
- A flight instructor in Liberty stations' docking bays swaps a perk for 2,000 credits per level.
- The character screen is now a pilots' ready room, with Juni standing there in 3D.
- New pilots start landed on Planet Manhattan.
- A banner announces when your standing with a faction turns hostile, neutral or friendly.
- Player Status shows changed factions on top, with crests beside each faction.
- Story-only factions no longer appear in the reputation list.
- Single player now runs entirely on your PC with its own saves; multiplayer characters are separate.

*World*

- Manhattan's surface is a full city, with a spaceport landing pad and an evening sky.
- Ships stream through lanes among Manhattan's towers.
- Manhattan's spaceport hub and a skyscraper block are Liberty white, with a Liberty star by the pad.
- The Skyline Lounge now stands on a Manhattan rooftop, with the city outside its windows.
- The Tahoe nebula in California is now wispy, see-through pale ice instead of a solid white cloud.
- NPC traffic now spawns zone by zone, filling the area as you launch, jump in or leave a lane.
- New York's lawful traffic is three times busier, with no more pirates.
- Trade lane rings can be disrupted, stopping rides and dropping ships out halfway.
- Hostile groups may ambush trade lanes, draining a ring's shield ahead of you.
- Dropping out of a lane now brakes and turns your ship off the lane.
- Trade lane rings glow in their faction's colour.
- Republican Shipping is now Rheinland Empire Shipping.
- Every faction now has a crest.

*Interface*

- The start menu offers NEW GAME, LOAD GAME, MULTIPLAYER, OPTIONS and EXIT.
- The start menu view looks down past Newark, its shadow cutting a sunbeam through the dust.
- The Flight Menu has a Main Menu option to switch pilot, save or realm.
- Planet landings and launches can be skipped with SKIP or Esc.
- The idle cinematic camera keeps playing in trade lanes and while docking.
- New system map filters mark bases with job boards or flight instructors.

*Graphics and performance*

- Options adds a Ray tracing switch; ray tracing now runs only with global illumination at High or Epic.
- Graphics quality now has four levels, Low to Epic.
- Quality presets now also scale fields, debris and nebulae.
- On first start, the game picks a quality preset and render scale to suit your PC.
- Nebulae run faster and use less graphics memory below Epic.
- Graphics memory use is lower everywhere.
- Engine exhausts now run only when visible, making the start menu and busy systems much faster.
- Distant engines, contrails and ship movement are cheaper, so big fights run much smoother.
- Countermeasure flares and missile trails cost far less, so fights with many flares stay smooth.
- Tractor beam, jump gate and teleport effects are cheaper and show their proper colours.
- Tractor beams glow in the crate's rarity colour.
- Trade lane ring effects no longer show a hard inner edge.
- Engines now light their own ship's hull, fins and wings, with shadows.
- Hull frost is reworked, with feathered edges and crystals, and now covers Rhino cargo containers.

*Sound*

- New afterburner sound.
- The start menu plays one of three menu tracks at random.
- Job results play victory or failure music; job pay plays the money sound.
- Escort and hold-the-line voices speak in their faction's accent, with a radio tone.

*Multiplayer*

- Jumps between servers no longer reload: the next system builds seamlessly under the jump vortex.
- PLAY joins your system's server directly and faster.
- The whole realm sees a banner when someone finds a Legendary.
- Looted wrecks stay looted even after a server restarts.

**New and changed in the [wiki](#/wiki)**

- New ship **[Startracker](#/wiki/ships/startracker)**: Boom strips' glow drawn from their slots' shape, one rectangular afterburner nozzle in place of the four small ports.
- New ship **[Patriot](#/wiki/ships/patriot)**: Patriot from the new police model.
- New ship **[Piranha](#/wiki/ships/piranha)**: The Piranha redesigned.
- New ship **[Transport](#/wiki/ships/transport)**: The companies' utility transport, 104 m, NPC only.
- New ship **[Large Transport](#/wiki/ships/large-transport)**: Now in the wiki.
- New ship **[Dagger](#/wiki/ships/dagger)**: The Dagger redesigned, with its two paints as liveries.
- New ship **[Wolfhound](#/wiki/ships/wolfhound)**: The Wolfhound redesigned, its intake fans turning.
- New weapon **[Barrager](#/wiki/weapons/barrager)**: The Junkers' gatling, the whole turret in one model.
- New weapon **[Scrapstorm](#/wiki/weapons/scrapstorm)**: Now in the wiki.
- New weapon **[Azrael](#/wiki/weapons/azrael)**: The Liberty Rogues' laser, a small mount on the Justice's base in its paint.
- New weapon **[Vassago](#/wiki/weapons/vassago)**: Now in the wiki.
- New weapon **[Exorcist](#/wiki/weapons/exorcist)**: Now in the wiki.
- New weapon **[Reaper](#/wiki/weapons/reaper)**: The Order's neutron cannon, the whole turret in one model, its turret line on its own base, the gun alone the barrel without it.
- New weapon **[Scorpion](#/wiki/weapons/scorpion)**: The Xenos' particle cannon, spiked black-rust armour with a scorpion's tail over its back, a gun alone on a medium mount, on the Justice's base in its paint.
- New weapon **[Tarantula](#/wiki/weapons/tarantula)**: Now in the wiki.
- New weapon **[Lavablade](#/wiki/weapons/lavablade)**: Liberty's heavy plasma gun, a large mount, its lava glowing.
- New weapon **[Starbeam](#/wiki/weapons/starbeam)**: The Starbeam's own model, and a turret base per gun line in that gun's colour.
- New weapon **[Stunpulse](#/wiki/weapons/stunpulse)**: The police EMP gun, a medium mount on the Justice's base in its paint.
- **[Rhino](#/wiki/ships/rhino)**: Patriot canopy panes as glass, the Rhino rebuilt, a new pilot starts landed on Manhattan.

posts.title: Multiple Ships, Liveries, and redoing it all again
posts.excerpt: Redoing the Starflier, Rhino and Defender, and multiple ships hangar!
posts.body:
# Never enough...

I have this issue that when I do something I demand absolute perfection from myself (and others (the AI lol)) and while it helps with details, it's not a healthy way to go about things :D

Either way, the closest to "perfect" I could've gotten was with Tripo AI modelling which turns images into wireframe models (textured) which I can then port 1:1 into the game.

Hence why now have the new Starflier:

![](images/uploads/2026-10-21-c02340c4-a134-4d0c-85c4-caec41025b44-mvi5j6v6.jpg)

New Rhino:

![](images/uploads/2026-10-21-image-mvi5jnqr.jpg)

And currently rebuilding the Defender:

![](images/uploads/2026-10-21-de60ae2b-6848-4444-a072-e3d82be5bfba-mvi5k7xy.jpg)

Ingame shots in the wiki soon.

Now I wanna redo the stations... man, it's not healthy :D

## Hangars, Multiple Ships and Liveries

Yes, you heard that right, multiple ships being owned will be possible. Well, it already is implemented :D Not a dream, it's already working.

With a storage where you can keep guns and cargo and whatnot.

![](images/uploads/2026-10-21-image-mvi5t2bn.jpg)

Icons are placeholders for now.

![](images/uploads/2026-10-21-image-mvi5tml2.jpg)


![](images/uploads/2026-10-21-image-mvi5u1hw.jpg)
Still gotta fix the nebulas in this one!


I also wanna put more effort into the trading system of the game because I thought the original lacked this a bit.

What else happened:
* Liveries for each ship per player are possible and already work (eventually I wanna add an editor so you can make em yourself)
* Player storage MMO baseline for the servers works
* NPC combat is in
* Friendly NPCs
* Redid the Trade lane VFX
* Missiles, torpedos, shields, all added to the game (no visuals yet)
* Main menu with graphics settings etc
* Redid the badlands nebula (again)
* Lots of bugfixes

posts.title: 0.2.1 we have a working New York and Rhino ALL NEW!
posts.excerpt: New York fully designed (minus some stations), that was some work!
posts.body:
# We have a website! And what a shitshow :D

This is the first post here, hurray! But Im not going to go all teary eyed on it.
Simple, I have been working quite a while on this.
5 days to be precise :D

It's truly remarkable how insanely fast modern AI can do things.

From just an idea a week ago I already have New York fully running in UE, all in a few days.

But this is not to say there wasn't a complete bullshittery going on.

But I have noticed why.

## The prompt is everything

Initially I used Grokbot, which is already a big mistake because Claude Code is SO MUCH better. Light years away.

I still use Grokbot for my local PC stuff. Very good at that and nicely integrated. But for coding, Claude is truly unbeaten.

However, due to that initial prompt that basically just moved the entire OLD way of how New York was built into UE, I was stuck with 20 year old lighting, scripts, and stations.

I only noticed this once I wanted to add better lighting in the nebulas, and it was virtually impossible to get right.

After many thousands of AI tokens I literally told Claude "Do this thing, and forget everything in the project so far, old tech, redo it entirely from scratch with UE" and then it worked.

So I ran an audit on the code and it basically told me it all sucks :D

Thus, the last 3 days I was pretty much busy having it rewrite the entire system from scratch with new coding methods.

## Current Status

Enough bullshitting. We got it going. The Defender is (mostly) done, Rhino is entirely rebuilt (see Screenshot), bunch of stations are here and NPCs fly around.

Concept:

![](images/uploads/2026-10-18-d5156cc7-ddd2-4f27-954c-f856c1827a8a-mve2toxh.jpg)

Ingame:

![](images/uploads/2026-10-18-cargo0-00-hero-mve4kihn.jpg)

![](images/uploads/2026-10-18-cargo1-09-engines-mve4krcg.jpg)

![](images/uploads/2026-10-18-cargo0-08-police-mve4lk6v.jpg)



As you can tell it's not exactly the concept, but I actually like how it came out. Considering this took the AI about 20min to do :D

Also notice the new effect, when your cargo is above 60% it visibly carries cargo in the midsection.

Defender Concept:

![](images/uploads/2026-10-18-927e85be-d4ac-4231-8493-1b7d37a0e806-mve2veru.jpg)


Ingame:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VKFcgTnifbc

This video is already old tho, lots of stuff missing.

Nebulas look fire, mines work, and currently I am building the planet surface for Pittsburgh which will be another shitshow, but here we are :D

-Alex
